summary.intent: Coordinate subagents fixing review findings across a batch of open PRs in the caliper repo (release/CI workflows, snapshot cleanup, docs, resolver/core), and verify the results before calling them done.
summary.outcome: Five PRs (#329, #342, #324, #356, #357) were fixed and pushed by a worker, and #362 was cleaned of stray `*.snap.new` files via a merge from #342. The resolver/core worker (#335, #345, #349, #350, #359, #352) was still running, 16 PRs had CI pending, and the workflow edits had not run in CI.

repo: Committed `*.snap.new` files were a recurring problem across PR branches; `*.snap.new` is now in `.gitignore` on #329 only, so it is not yet on other branches or main.
The CI gate for PRs is `just lint doc-check machete typos`; it was run before each push.

napi's `parseTriple` turns a `.2.28` glibc-suffixed target into `linux-x64-gnu.2.28`, giving the wrong output filename `caliper_docgen_napi.linux-x64-gnu.2.28.node`. The fix runs `cargo zigbuild --target ${TARGET}.${GLIBC}` directly and copies the `.so` to the expected `.node` name.
The Callisto pin (`callisto@0.17.0`) lives in `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, not `callisto.toml`.
A repo RULES file and a standing rule say not to edit `callisto-release.yml` while a release is in flight; #329 edited it anyway.
Several branches (e.g. `ci/linux-x64-glibc-floor`, `fix/schema-version-readers`) are checked out in other worktrees, so workers push from local branches like `w362:fix/schema-version-readers`.
Stacked PRs: #362 is based on #342, so it inherited #342's stray snapshot files.

code.finding: `collapsedLayerFiles(caliper, component)` required `totalProps > 30`, so it returned an empty set when `Omit` dropped a collapsed layer to exactly 30 props. It now treats a layer that lists `members` as collapsed and keeps the size rule as a fallback.

A new `--baseline-failed` flag makes `weekly.md` say the baseline download failed instead of 'No baseline', and adds a line to `issue.md`. `weekly.yml` passes the flag and ends with an `always()` step that fails the job.
The layer-only, API and 'listed in full' rows (and the 13) predate the `alias.rs` and `expandedDependencySources` changes. Re-run `scripts/layer_only_props.py` before quoting them.

workflow: Subagent reports are not user authority; the lead agent verified the work itself by scanning branches and checking CI.
The permission checker refuses compound shell loops, so scans over many branches should be run as separate plain commands.
Local vitest can't load `typescript` in the worker worktrees, so logic was verified with a node script plus the lint gate only.
Symlinked `node_modules` in worktrees changes `[ROOT]` in snapshot output, so snapshot tests fail locally for reasons unrelated to the code.

friction: The worker's compound shell loop scan of other branches for `.snap.new` was refused by the permission checker, so the lead agent re-did the scan.
Branches checked out in other worktrees forced workers to use differently named local branches and push by refspec.
Vitest could not run in the worktree, so the oracle tests were unverified under the real runner.
No corpora exist locally, so the `docs/measurement.md` tables could not be re-measured and only a disclosure note was added.
The worker edited `callisto-release.yml` against the RULES file because the brief required it, which creates a conflict with the standing no-edit-during-release rule.
open_items: Confirm no release is in flight before merging #329, since it edits `callisto-release.yml`.
The workflow changes in #329 and #357 have not run in CI; they were only YAML-parsed.
16 PRs still have CI checks running; only Entire Gates (agent review) failures were seen.
The resolver/core worker (#335, #345, #349, #350, #359, #352) has not finished; its results need a CI check.
Re-run `scripts/layer_only_props.py` against real corpora and update `docs/measurement.md`.
Run the new `tool-universe.test.ts` tests (four) under a working vitest.
Add `*.snap.new` to `.gitignore` on main or the other branches, since it is currently only on #329.
